unit: documentation claim vs repository reality; artifact classes are external domain concepts, not engine predicates
principle: external-first harvest, maximal, NO de-duplication: one row per (source, source_label); original labels preserved verbatim; canonicalization is a separate overlay (normalization.json). Method/behavior/process/data rows are KEPT with unit/scope tags.
notes: Predicate names of the engine must not appear as a selection axis (validate_catalog.py enforces this).
The 'ours' layer (catalog_ours.json) is added only AFTER this layer is frozen, from incidents in our own runs and real bug reports, never from the engine's predicates.

Harvest status per source: readu=complete, mpc_2025=complete(paper), docprism=complete(paper), vasperabench=complete(dataset card), truth_benchmark=complete(repo README), dca_bench=partial(abstract/table), cascade=complete(local notes), docchecker=complete(binary), aghajani_2019=partial(top-level only; figure not machine-readable), wen_2019=partial(top-level only), docer=partial(described via READU driver), readme_auto_update=partial.

docchecker.ref: DocChecker (EACL 2024 demos); local other_instruments/DocChecker and CASCADE driver

aghajani_2019.ref: Aghajani et al., 'Software Documentation Issues Unveiled', 2019

wen_2019.ref: Wen et al., 'A Large-Scale Empirical Study on Code-Comment Inconsistencies', ICPC 2019

docer.ref: DOCER (Tan, Wagner, Treude); driver in CASCADE/PaperEvaluation/drivers/Docer and READU regex_list.txt

entries.definition: Documentation claims about repository-internal code, APIs, defaults, types, supported options or behavior no longer match the implementation.

examples.quote: Documentation states clamav_max_concurrency default is 5 but code defaults to 10
README says header overhead is ~88 bytes but show.go was updated to ~150 bytes per tensor blob
code has renamed field to mmap_prepare but doc still describes mmap

entries.definition: Documentation depends on external resources, package APIs, names, model registries, URLs, versions, or platform/tool behavior.

examples.quote: Model ID z-ai/glm-5v-turbo does not exist on OpenRouter's model registry
Italian translation states minimum Rust version 1.78.0, but actual minimum is 1.85.0

entries.definition: A current-state API/feature exists in code but is absent or incomplete in the documentation.

examples.quote: mxfp4 quantization type is supported by the code but not documented in the blob format spec
API guide 'Available Scopes' table is missing WRITE_GRAPH and WRITE_LIBRARY permissions

entries.source_label: Invalid Copy-Paste Code, Command, or Setup Instructions
entries.definition: A documented code example, command, or setup instruction no longer works.

examples.quote: Installation instructions claim k6 is available via 'sudo apt-get install k6', but it is not in default Debian/Ubuntu repos
Codex CLI >=v0.135.0 rejects bare `codex --oss` with an error, contradicting the docs

entries.definition: Two documents (or a document and its translation) make contradictory statements, or a name used for an entity drifts.

examples.quote: Documentation/PCI/pci.rst references acenic driver which was removed
README contradicts itself and the code about the default number of generated tokens (150+ vs 10)

entries.definition: Spelling/grammar/copy-editing issues with no factual consequence.

examples.quote: The new table row uses 'NVIDIA Professioal' (typo) while all other rows use 'NVIDIA Professional'

entries.definition: A real or plausible inconsistency that already existed before the evaluated commit (not commit-induced).

examples.quote: README's Node 16.x prerequisite was already stale vs newer Node/pnpm requirements

entries.definition: Checker matched a doc claim to the wrong implementation detail or missed inherited/global behavior.

examples.quote: Github Update File docs list error as an output but error is inherited from BlockSchemaOutput

entries.definition: Documentation is an example/partial list/high-level guide rather than an exhaustive API spec; missing items are not bugs.

examples.quote: The README only documents --quantize fp8 but the code now supports both fp4 and fp8 (README doesn't have to be exhaustive)

entries.definition: Acceptable wording differences, equivalent commands/syntax, optional steps or harmless duplication are not contradictions.

examples.quote: docs reference localhost:11434 but code defaults to 127.0.0.1 (same host)

entries.source_label: Incorrect External Evidence or Source of Truth
entries.definition: The external checker used an incomplete or incorrect external fact.

examples.quote: Docs claim OpenSAML requires Shibboleth repo, but the versions used are not on Maven Central, so the repo remains required

entries.definition: If the part is factually incorrect, it is a README bug.
If the part is not up-to-date when it should be, it is a README bug (docs assumed current by default).
If the part is incomplete when it should be complete, it is a README bug; wording like 'example/such as/including/for instance' signals incompleteness is intended.
A commit-induced README bug is a README bug caused by the commit being triaged; pre-existing bugs are controls.

entries.source_label: Doc-Only Repairs for Multi-Artifact Upstream Fixes
entries.definition: Repair failure: doc-only fix for an issue that requires multi-artifact upstream changes.
Repair failure: the generated repair is incomplete or under-specified.
Repair failure: wrong replacement text or mismatched root cause.
Repair failure: no usable patch generated.
Repair failure: patch weakens a contract or is over-destructive.

entries.source_label: potential_readme_bug_scenarios: env var / feature flag / config option
entries.definition: Documentation lists an env var / feature flag / config option that no longer exists, or omits one that was added.

examples.quote: README lists feature flags including NEW_BLOCK_MENU, GRAPH_SEARCH, AGENT_FAVORITING; those flags no longer exist
Setup docs that list environment variables will be incomplete without documenting NEXT_PUBLIC_FORCE_FLAG_* overrides

entries.definition: A documented HTTP/API endpoint path was renamed/removed or a new endpoint is undocumented.

examples.quote: README references the old onboarding API endpoint /api/onboarding/enabled, replaced by /api/onboarding/completed
README lists available API endpoints but omits the new /api/copilot/admin/rate_limit endpoints

entries.definition: A documented API request/response field was added, removed, renamed or had its semantics changed.

examples.quote: README shows CredentialSummary model but API now returns CredentialsMetaResponse
README states GET /credentials returns full credential objects including secrets; now returns CredentialsMetaResponse without secrets

entries.source_label: potential_readme_bug_scenarios: UI strings / entity naming drift
entries.definition: A user-visible name (agent name, UI label, path component) changed while docs keep the old name.

examples.quote: README refers to the agent as 'Otto' but the UI now says 'AutoPilot is ready'

entries.source_label: potential_readme_bug_scenarios: quoted error message string changed
entries.definition: Documentation quotes an exact error message string that changed in code (candidate; not observed in confirmed READU TPs).

examples.quote: README documents error message 'Credentials do not match the specified provider' which now returns 'Credentials not found'

entries.definition: A documented command or its flags changed in code/build.

examples.quote: README describes running tests with 'vitest run' but frontend now uses 'vitest run --coverage'

entries.definition: A documented file/directory location no longer matches the repository tree.

evidence.ref: pre_filter scenarios + READU_tp.md Implementation-Documentation Drift examples

examples.quote: getting-started.md says the Makefile is 'in the repo root', but the Makefile is at autogpt_platform/Makefile
Flow.tsx is listed at the root of FlowEditor in docs but was moved to Flow/Flow.tsx
docs/content/index.md links to platform/new_blocks.md which no longer exists after files were moved

entries.definition: A documented set of allowed values/model names/architectures no longer matches code.

examples.quote: LLM providers guide lists model name 'Llama-3-70B-Instruct' but the code defines it as 'Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct'
README example uses Flag.AGENT_ACTIVITY which was removed from the Flag enum
docs list q8_0 and q4_0 as available K/V cache quantization types, but code now rejects them for gpt-oss

entries.definition: A documented type/format of an output or field differs from code.

examples.quote: Documentation lists the result output type as 'Result', but the implementation defines it as 'Any'
llm.md lists sandbox_id output type as 'str' but code defines it as 'Optional[str]'

entries.definition: A localized/translated copy of a document diverges from the canonical document.

evidence.ref: READU_tp.md Cross-Document, Translation, or Naming Drift

examples.quote: Italian translation states minimum Rust version 1.78.0 while the English doc lists 1.85.0

entries.source_label: The commit directly changes README-like documentation
entries.definition: Not a bug class: the prefilter heuristic routing any commit that touches docs; excluded from classes but recorded as the dominant repeated scenario.
A documented throws/exception contract no longer matches the implementation.

examples.quote: changed an exception type
thrown exepction is removed

entries.definition: Documented null/absent-value behavior changed.

examples.quote: changed meanign of null
added extra behavior if null

entries.definition: Documented representation, format, encoding, or unit differs from code.

examples.quote: the input string uses a different encoding mechanism than the one in the description
changed date parse regex

entries.definition: Documented comparison polarity or ordering is reversed relative to code.

examples.quote: before and after switched
say "do not match" instead of "match"

entries.definition: Documented precondition/lifecycle guarantee (must-close, mandatory, parent-free) changed.

examples.quote: says that input has to be closed after but actually already does that automatically
if an argument is required -> whether this Option is mandatory

entries.source_label: return type / default-range / membership / identifier / missing throws / example (method-level)
entries.definition: CASCADE notes that map to existing repo-level classes but are instantiated at method level.

examples.quote: completly changes return type
changed default value of a attribute
added undocumented throws

entries.source_label: return-value semantics / edge-case clarity / copy-paste / typo-induced
entries.definition: Method-level behavior/return-value or clarity changes, not decidable against a repo artifact inventory.

examples.quote: returns string -> returns normlaized string
completly wrong doc probably copy paste

entries.definition: Binary code-comment consistency verdict; no error-class taxonomy.
A parameter was renamed; documentation still names the old one.
A constraint/default value changed while documentation states the old value.

examples.quote: doc states trend/seasonal use 'and' but code uses 'or'

entries.definition: Documented logic/behaviour diverges from code.
A parameter was removed while documentation still documents it.
New inter-parameter constraints exist in code but are undocumented.
Inter-parameter constraints were removed from code but remain documented.
A parameter/constraint is undocumented.
A parameter description was modified so it no longer matches code.
Features described in docs logically conflict with the implementation.
Documented parameters absent from signature, or signature params undocumented.
A documented parameter type differs from code.
An identifier named in docs differs from code.
Documented return type differs from code.
A feature specified in docs is absent from code.
Documented parameters are not used in the code body.
Values differ (rate limits, timeouts).

examples.quote: Doc: free tier = 100, Code: free = 50

entries.definition: API signature changed relative to docs.
Implementation differs from docs.
Doc mentions a param not in code.
Code has a param not in docs.
Type differs between doc and code.
Security-related drift.
Configuration value mismatch.

examples.quote: /api/config: docs say 1 hour, code has max-age=1800 (30 min)

entries.definition: Code exists without documentation.
Documentation describes unimplemented features.
Code uses a wrong operator/constant relative to the claim.

examples.quote: claim 'deletes files'; os.remove(path) MATCH vs open(path,'w').write('') LIE

entries.definition: Code omits a security property the claim asserts.

examples.quote: claim 'encrypts password before storing'; bcrypt.hash(...) MATCH vs db.save(user, password) LIE

entries.definition: Code sorts/uses a protocol contrary to the claim.

entries.source_label: subtle traps (byte vs char length, set vs dict.fromkeys, soft vs hard delete, indexOf>0)
entries.definition: Plausible but subtly wrong implementations.
Typographical errors in dataset/documentation.
Wrong file/content format.
Inappropriate file present.
Conflicting information within a file.
Conflicting information between files.
Documentation with wrong or insufficient information.
Dataset content defects, not documentation↔code.

entries.source_label: Information content (what is written) - incl. Correctness
entries.definition: Issues about what documentation says (accuracy, content); 'Correctness' is the largest subcategory.

evidence.ref: abstract + taxonomy (162 types across 4 categories); Correctness = 72 artifacts

entries.definition: Issues about how content is presented and organized.
Issues about the documentation process (who/when/why).
Issues about documentation tool support.

entries.source_label: code-comment inconsistency types fixed by developers (triggered by code changes)
entries.definition: Taxonomy of code-comment inconsistencies fixed by developers; types of code changes that trigger comment updates.

evidence.ref: abstract (503 commits manually analyzed; 1.3B AST changes mined)

entries.source_label: stale code-element reference (occurrence drops to zero: deletion or rename)
entries.definition: A code element referenced in README/wiki is no longer present (deleted or renamed).

evidence.artifact: DOCER (Tan/Wagner/Treude) as described in README related work and READU driver

entries.source_label: README should be updated alongside a code change
entries.definition: Just-in-time check that a single top-level README stays consistent with a code change.
